title: Release audit: Quoted secret labels are not fully redacted. For a message such as `'token': 'ab
summary: Handle a closing quote after a quoted label before looking for the separator, or parse quoted keys and values; add tests for quoted labels and JSON snippets and assert the value is absent from captured output.
requirements: When a message contains a secret label enclosed in matching single quotation marks, followed by a separator and a value, the displayed text keeps the label and both of its quotation marks as they are, keeps the separator as it is, and replaces the value with the masking placeholder.

When a message contains a secret label enclosed in matching double quotation marks, including the JSON-style form where the label's closing quote is directly followed by a colon, the displayed text keeps the label and both of its quotation marks and the separator as they are, and replaces the value with the masking placeholder.
When the value of a quoted secret label is itself quoted, the value's own quotation marks stay visible around the masking placeholder and no character of the value remains.
When the value of a quoted secret label is unquoted, the whole value up to the next whitespace or the end of the message is replaced by the masking placeholder.
No character of a secret bound to a quoted label appears in any text the session displays, including reply text, engine state and engine error text.
Masking a message that is already masked changes nothing further.
Each masked value carries exactly one masking placeholder, and repeated separator characters between a quoted label and its value stay visible.
A message with no secret bound to a label, and a message that only mentions a secret label without binding a value to it, is displayed unchanged.
The quotation marks that a fix introduces as part of the label never cause a neighbouring word, a separator or trailing punctuation to be masked.

The automated test suite covers a single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value, a double-quoted secret label with a double-quoted value, and the JSON-style form where the label's closing quote is directly followed by the separator.
The existing test suite continues to pass without any test being weakened, skipped or deleted.
acceptance: A session line carrying a single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value displays the label and its quotes, the separator, and the masking placeholder in place of the value; searching the displayed line for the value finds nothing.

A session line carrying a double-quoted secret label with a double-quoted value, in the form where the label's closing quote is directly followed by a colon, displays the label and its quotes, the colon, and the masking placeholder in place of the value; searching the displayed line for the value finds nothing.
A single-quoted secret label followed by an unquoted value displays the value replaced by a single masking placeholder, with nothing of the value left and no neighbouring word masked.
Masking an already masked message that carries a quoted secret label leaves it unchanged, and each masked value carries exactly one masking placeholder.
Messages without a secret binding, and messages that only mention a secret label, are displayed unchanged.
The automated test suite contains passing checks for the single-quoted form, the double-quoted form and the JSON-style form, and the whole suite passes.
plan_goal: Forgel Code: interactive agent client instead of a command wrapper

checks.criterion: A single-quoted secret label with a single-quoted value is masked in full when displayed.
A double-quoted secret label with a double-quoted value in the JSON-style form is masked in full when displayed.
An unquoted value after a quoted secret label is masked with exactly one placeholder and no neighbouring word masked.
Masking is idempotent and each masked value carries exactly one placeholder.
Secret-free text and label-only mentions are displayed unchanged.
The suite covers the single-quoted, double-quoted and JSON-style forms and the whole suite passes.

result.summary: Extended the session masking so a secret label wrapped in matching quotation marks is recognised as a label rather than as the opening quote of its value. `forgel_code/interactive.py` gains `_label_quote_end`, which decides that a quote after a label closes the label when no value character touches it (a separator, whitespace, punctuation or end of message follows), and `_quoted_binding`, which takes the value bound to that quoted label through `=`/`:` separators or as an adjacent quoted run; `_binding` now consults both before falling back to the previous behaviour. Quoted labels therefore keep the label, both of its quotes, the separator and any repeated separators visible, while the value is replaced by the single `[redacted]` placeholder — inside the value's own quotes when the value is quoted, up to the next whitespace when it is not. `tests/test_redact.py` adds coverage for the single-quoted label with a single-quoted value, the double-quoted label with a double-quoted value, the JSON-style form (`{"token":"abc123"}`), an unquoted value after a quoted label, repeated separators, non-masking of neighbouring words and trailing punctuation, idempotence and exactly-one-placeholder for the quoted forms, absence of any value character, and a session-level reply carrying a quoted label. Full suite: `python -m pytest -q` -> 297 passed, 262 subtests passed.
assumptions: A quoted value belongs to the quoted label as a whole: the marker sits inside the value's own quotes, so the rest of the quoted run is masked too, matching the existing behaviour for unquoted labels with quoted values (`password: "hunter2 and more"`).
A quoted label binds a value only through an `=`/`:` separator or an immediately adjacent quoted run; a plain word after the closing quote still counts as a mention and stays visible.
